chunks: Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn al-Sindi from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-A'la, the freedman of the family of Sam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no divorce except according to the Book of Allah, and no manumission except for the sake of Allah."

key_terms.لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ: For the sake of Allah (sincerely for God)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid divorce and manumission according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Reported by Aban ibn Uthman in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this concise hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the dual requirement of legal compliance and spiritual sincerity in key acts of worship. It reinforces the Shia jurisprudential view that while divorce must adhere to the procedural framework of the Quran, manumission is elevated by being performed purely for divine pleasure, linking legal validity (sahha) with spiritual merit (thawab).
